speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These are concerning systemic symptoms; to start our investigation, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation or diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those "drenching night sweats" and significant weight loss are very concerning; given the location of your enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, is the abdominal pain specifically in the right upper quadrant, and do you have any history of alcohol use or jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that the lymph nodes feel "fixed" and non-tender is highly alarming for malignancy. Have you noticed any lumps in your armpits or groin, and have you been exposed to anyone recently diagnosed with tuberculosis? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and peripheral smear.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC shows a leukocytosis with a slightly low hemoglobin, which confirms a systemic process. Given the "fixed" supraclavicular nodes and your abdominal pain, have you noticed any painless lumps in your neck, or any difficulty swallowing or breathing? REQUEST TEST: Liver function tests (LFTs) and LDH.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), "fixed" supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain, and significantly elevated LDH is highly suggestive of an aggressive lymphoid malignancy. The slightly low hemoglobin also indicates bone marrow involvement or chronic disease. I will proceed to biopsy the node to confirm.
